title: TEXTILE RECYCLING AND CIRCULAR ECONOMY
body_text:
The Government has undertaken several initiatives to promote textile recycling, adoption of recycling technologies and the transition towards a circular economy in the textile sector:
i) In the Union Budget 2026–27, the Hon'ble Finance Minister announced the ‘Tex-Eco Initiative’ to promote a globally competitive and sustainable textiles and apparel sector. The initiative aims to support innovative technologies for the circular economy, including textile waste management, recycling and value addition, development of recycled fibres, new materials, sustainable packaging and other high-value products from discarded textiles, in collaboration with research institutions, Textile Research Associations, Centres of Excellence, industry, start-ups and other stakeholders.
ii) The Ministry of Textiles has undertaken a study titled “Mapping of Textile Waste Value Chain in India”. The report estimates the generation of textile waste from pre-consumer sources such as manufacturing waste as well as post-consumer waste.
iii) The Government has also constituted an Environment, Social and Governance (ESG) Task Force to deliberate on sustainable production, certification and exports, besides facilitating industry-centric programmes such as Circular Samvaad and the Cluster Exchange Mechanism.
iv) The Government is also promoting textile recycling and sustainable manufacturing through policy support, research, innovation and capacity-building initiatives, including:
The UNIDO-Global Environment Facility (GEF) project on eliminating hazardous chemicals from the textile fashion supply chain; The UNEP supported In-Tex India Project for Accelerating the Transition of the Indian Textile Sector towards Circularity using Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and Product Environmental Footprint (PEF); Support for environmentally sustainable research and development under the National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM); Development of a sustainability framework for PM MITRA Parks; and Promotion of upcycled products in Government procurement through an MoU among the Textiles Committee, Standing Conference of Public Enterprises (SCOPE) and Government e-Marketplace (GeM).
These initiatives are sector-wide and are intended to facilitate technology adoption, research, innovation, sustainable manufacturing and circular economy practices across the textile value chain.
This information was provided by THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today.
*****
MAM/VN
(Lok Sabha US Q3899)

enrichment.summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Textiles outlined government measures to promote textile recycling and a circular economy, including the Union Budget 2026-27's 'Tex-Eco Initiative', a study mapping India's textile waste value chain, an ESG Task Force, and various international and domestic projects like UNIDO-GEF, UNEP In-Tex India, NTTM support, PM MITRA Parks sustainability framework, and promotion of upcycled products via GeM procurement.
enrichment.context:
Textile waste management and circularity have become pressing global and domestic concerns as the textile and apparel sector is among the most resource-intensive and polluting industries, generating significant pre-consumer (manufacturing) and post-consumer waste. India, as one of the world's largest textile producers and exporters, faces both an opportunity and a challenge in aligning its industry with global sustainability standards (such as EU's upcoming Extended Producer Responsibility and eco-design regulations for textiles) to remain competitive in export markets. The 'Tex-Eco Initiative' announced in Budget 2026-27 reflects this push, building on earlier flagship schemes like the PM MITRA Parks (mega integrated textile parks) and the National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM), which already have components for technology upgradation and sustainability.

This also ties into India's broader environmental commitments, including its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and circular economy action plans under NITI Aayog, as textiles recycling reduces landfill burden, virgin fibre consumption, and carbon footprint. International collaborations with UNIDO, GEF, and UNEP indicate India's participation in global sustainable-supply-chain frameworks, particularly around hazardous chemical elimination and Life Cycle Assessment methodologies, which are increasingly used as non-tariff standards in global trade. The ESG Task Force and mechanisms like Circular Samvaad and Cluster Exchange are part of a broader governance push to make sustainability reporting and certification standardized across India's textile clusters, many of which are dominated by MSMEs lacking resources for compliance.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Tex-Eco Initiative', aimed at promoting a sustainable and circular textiles economy, was announced in which of the following?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the PIB release, the Hon'ble Finance Minister announced the 'Tex-Eco Initiative' in the Union Budget 2026-27 to support circular economy technologies in the textile sector.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding India's textile recycling initiatives as highlighted by the Ministry of Textiles:
1. The UNIDO-GEF project focuses on eliminating hazardous chemicals from the textile-fashion supply chain.
2. The In-Tex India Project is supported by UNEP and uses Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methodology.
3. PM MITRA Parks have no sustainability framework component.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release confirms statements 1 and 2 as accurate; however, it explicitly mentions development of a sustainability framework for PM MITRA Parks, making statement 3 incorrect.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of promoting a circular economy in India's textile sector. Examine the key government initiatives aimed at achieving this transition and the challenges likely to be faced by MSMEs in adopting sustainable practices.

India's textile exports face increasing scrutiny under global sustainability and environmental standards. Analyze how initiatives like the Tex-Eco Initiative and international collaborations (UNIDO-GEF, UNEP) can help India align with these standards while maintaining competitiveness.
